original_question: Let A be a pseudo-amenable Banach algebra, or an approximately amenable Banach algebra that already has an approximate identity. Under what additional conditions must a closed ideal of A have a two-sided approximate identity?
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, Question 10: "Let A be pseudo-amenable or be approximately amenable with an approximate identity. When does a closed ideal of A have a two-sided approximate identity?"
correct_elements: Your draft has identified the correct target almost exactly: it is the paper's Question 10 in the ideals section. It has the right ambient object (a Banach algebra A), the right two hypotheses on A (pseudo-amenable, or approximately amenable together with an approximate identity), the right subobject (a closed ideal), and the right issue (existence of a two-sided approximate identity for that ideal).
missing_details: The paper states this as an open question, not as a theorem or conjecture with a specified answer.
The ideal should be introduced explicitly, say J, and in this context it should be understood as a closed two-sided ideal.
To make the question stand alone, the meanings of "pseudo-amenable" and "approximately amenable" should be stated, since they are defined earlier in the paper rather than inside Question 10 itself.
The phrase "two-sided approximate identity" should be made explicit: a net (e_beta) in J such that e_beta x -> x and x e_beta -> x for every x in J.

The paper does not strengthen the hypothesis "A has an approximate identity" to "A has a bounded approximate identity"; that distinction matters, because bounded approximate identities interact with pseudo-amenability via Theorem 2.7.

Nearby context should be reflected: Theorem 3.10 only yields one-sided approximate identities for ideals under complementedness assumptions, and the unresolved point is when one can obtain a genuine two-sided approximate identity.

The phrase "under what additional conditions" is slightly less faithful than the paper's "When does..."; the official formulation asks for a characterization or sharp sufficient hypotheses in general, not for one preselected extra assumption.
refined_question: Let A be a Banach algebra and J a closed two-sided ideal of A. Assume either: (i) A is pseudo-amenable, meaning that there exists a net (u_alpha) in A \hat{\otimes} A such that a u_alpha - u_alpha a -> 0 and \pi(u_alpha)a -> a for every a in A; or (ii) A is approximately amenable, meaning that for every Banach A-bimodule X and every continuous derivation D: A -> X* there exists a net (m_i) in X* with D(a) = lim_i (a·m_i - m_i·a) for all a in A, and moreover A has an approximate identity. Under what conditions must J have a two-sided approximate identity, i.e. a net (e_beta) in J such that e_beta x -> x and x e_beta -> x for every x in J?
justification: The draft is targeting Question 10 almost verbatim. The relevant definitions are the paper's Definition 1.2 (approximately amenable) and Definition 1.3 (pseudo-amenable). The nearby context in Section 3.1 explains why approximate identities are central: pseudo-amenable algebras automatically have a two-sided approximate identity, while approximately amenable algebras are only known in general to have left and right approximate identities (Theorem 3.3 and Question 4). Then Section 3.3 gives partial ideal results in Theorem 3.10, guaranteeing one-sided approximate identities for certain left/right ideals under complementedness assumptions; immediately after noting that even for two-sided ideals this still does not yield a genuine two-sided approximate identity, the paper asks Question 10. Theorem 2.7 is also nearby relevant context because it shows that replacing "approximate identity" by "bounded approximate identity" would materially change the scope of the question.
